title: [field] Fix custom validity ownership and validation lifecycle

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

body:
Establishes explicit ownership of the `setCustomValidity` messages the field installs, and fixes four validation bugs that trace back to the missing ownership model. First of a series from a full review of the Form/Field module.

## Changes

- The field records each custom validity message it installs (per input, matched on normalized text) and retires its own residue at the start of every validation pass. Previously the stale message read back through `element.validationMessage` as if it were a native constraint, so with `validationMode="onBlur"` a cross-field validator (confirm password) never re-ran on submit and the form stayed blocked until the user retyped in that field.
- Messages set outside the field are preserved: the field never clears them, restores a message its own error displaced once that error resolves, and treats an overwrite or withdrawal by outside code as an ownership transfer. This supersedes #5348: it covers the same scenario and fixes the gaps flagged in its review, including ownership on inputs barred from constraint validation (disabled or readonly), where `validationMessage` is unreadable.
- Validator results are normalized once: `null`, `undefined`, `''`, and `[]` are valid. `validate={() => []}` previously marked the field invalid with an empty visible `Field.Error` and a permanently blocked submit.
- Published validity is built in one place, so `valid: true` can no longer coexist with a non-empty `errors` array (previously observable through `Field.Validity` for a pristine required field in `onBlur` mode).
- Pending validation dies with its control: a debounced or async validation is canceled when the registered control unmounts or is replaced, and starting an async validation synchronously retires the previous result from the form registry so a stale error cannot block submission (async validation is documented not to block it).

## Notes

Two existing tests depended on the `[]`/`undefined` bug to keep their forms from actually submitting in the browser test env. They now call `preventDefault` explicitly, matching their intent (asserting `formValues`).
